_note: Skeleton for docs/ledger-retirements.json — the factory data file read by tests/test_close_row_revision.py. Copy it into docs/ (the example itself is never read) and add an entry ONLY for a ledger row whose declared revision is known NOT to resolve: the ledger is append-only, so a false token cannot be removed, only NAMED by a later row. Each entry retires ONE field of ONE row and carries five values — the row, the field, the false value it declares, the NAMING ROW, and the true value. The naming row is what makes a retirement auditable: it is the row that says 'this value was wrong and here is the right one', so an entry whose naming row the ledger does not carry is a gate ERROR, never a silent pass. The entry is ADMITTED only when the ledger carries its naming row AND that row's detail carries the false value VERBATIM; an entry that matches no unresolvable token is an ERROR too, because it would inflate the visible debt while excusing nothing. Every admitted entry is printed as a 'retired:' line on EVERY gate run, so clean / excused / retired are three DIFFERENT outputs and never the same one.
